sections.title: Why the Roadmap Must Be a File

paragraphs.first_sentence: Every team I have watched lose a quarter lost it the same way.
paragraphs.heading_overlap_sentence: This essay argues that a plan which is not a file under version control is not a plan.

sections.title: The plan lives where the work lives

paragraphs.first_sentence: A plan written in a document nobody opens is a plan nobody follows.
paragraphs.heading_overlap_sentence: A plan written in a document nobody opens is a plan nobody follows.
When the plan changes, the diff says what changed and the commit says why.

sections.title: What breaks when the plan drifts

paragraphs.first_sentence: However, a file alone is not enough.
paragraphs.heading_overlap_sentence: A version bump without a note in the plan is the common case, and it is silent: the code says 0.7.0, the plan says 0.6.0, and nothing complains.

paragraphs.first_sentence: So the check has to be mechanical.
paragraphs.heading_overlap_sentence: Nobody remembered to update the plan; the build refused to pass until they did.

sections.title: The objection, and why it fails

paragraphs.first_sentence: The usual objection is that a mechanical check makes people update the plan without thinking.
paragraphs.heading_overlap_sentence: The usual objection is that a mechanical check makes people update the plan without thinking.

limits: Topic-sentence candidates are positional (first sentence) and lexical (highest heading overlap); neither is a semantic judgement.
Claim markers are counts of listed word classes, not a claim detector; the lists are in the tool and are the whole definition.
A transition is a listed opening marker, a demonstrative, or content-word overlap ≥ 0.08 with the previous paragraph; absence of all three is reported, not judged.
Sections are ATX headings; a document with other structure reads as one preamble section.
Sentence boundaries are an English heuristic with a finite abbreviation list.
A capitalised run is a surface pattern, not a named entity; sentence-initial function words are excluded by a stoplist, nothing else is.
Defined terms are matched by three surface patterns ('X is', 'X, the', 'called X').
Dates are recognised in numeric and month-name forms only.
Markdown structure recognised: ATX headings, fenced and inline code, links, frontmatter, list and quote markers, tables, thematic breaks.
